name: Ndobo
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Motingea Mangulu, André (1990) Esquisse du parler des Ndobo, Annales Aequatoria 11 (grammar sketch; not online)

sources.note: Bibliographic record only: classification refs Motingea 1996: 185-189 and Bastin, Coupez & Mann 1999: 205; sole descriptive ref is the 1990 sketch.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Esquisse du parler des Ndobo. In: Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale (Etudes Aequatoria 8), pp. 254-273. Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. [open athttps://www.aequatoria.be/publications/assets/Etudes_Aequatoria_8_parlers_riverains.pdf]
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. I 'Phonologie' pp. 254-256 (page scan read) has only 1. Voyelles (7 /i e ɛ a ɔ o u/), 2. Consonnes with remarks, 3. Phénomènes vocaliques (harmonie progressive, dévocalisation, coalescence, élision). No tonology subsection, no word on accent/stress anywhere in pp. 254-273 (only 'ils portent généralement un ton haut' about pronominal prefixes). Volume conclusion p. 275 concedes 'un certain nombre de lacunes décelables surtout au niveau de la tonologie'.

sources.citation: Donzo Bunza Yugia, Jean-Pierre. 2015. Langues bantoues de l'entre Congo-Ubangi (RD Congo): documentation, reconstruction, classification et contacts avec les langues oubanguiennes. PhD, Université Libre de Bruxelles.
sources.note: Ndobo appears only as a language name in a citation of Motingea (1996) on *p loss (pp. 155-156) and as the lexeme ndobo 'hameçon'; no Ndobo phonology, nothing on Ndobo stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André & Bonzoi Mwamakasa. 2008. Aux sources du lingála: cas du mbenga de Mankanza – Nouvel Anvers. African Study Monographs Suppl. 38: 1-93.

sources.note: Mbenga (Mabaale) description; Ndobo named only in neighbour/classification lists; no Ndobo data and no accent statement (only 'accent aigu/circonflexe' as tone-diacritic names).

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 2001. Etat de la recherche en linguistique descriptive sur les langues du Congo, dix ans après Kadima Kamuleta. Annales Aequatoria 22: 125-136. doi:10.4314/aq.v22i1.5588 (whole volume downloaded from aequatoria.be)
sources.note: Bibliographic survey only; its 'Groupe C.30' list (pp. 127-128) names no Ndobo description beyond the 1990 volume and Motingea 1996 (CNWS 43). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1989. Sur les parlers riverains de la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 281-283.
sources.note: Three-page classification note (Libinza/Bobangi/Motembo/Bamwe/Zamba subgroups); nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1991. Notes mabembe (bantou C30). Frankfurter Afrikanistische Blätter 3: 14-33.

sources.note: Mabembe is a sister lect in the same Libinza subgroup (Motingea 1990: 221); if it carries an accent statement it would be the nearest proxy, though not Ndobo itself.

sources.note: Comparative phonology/morphology of the Ngiri lects including Ndobo (pp. 185-189 per Glottolog; Donzo 2015 cites it for Ndobo *p loss); the only other work known to treat Ndobo and the likeliest place for a general prosody (tone/accent) statement covering the Libinza subgroup.
